title: Span Budget Sprint Digest: Adaptive Sampling Spike
content:
Summary:

Short sprint digest for the week focused on cost-aware tracing: we ran an adaptive sampling spike, instrumented a small subset of routes with per-route rate caps, and kicked off a dashboard migration to a columnar metrics store for cheaper long-term retention. The immediate goal was to shave span ingestion costs without losing signal for the high-variance routes.

Key outcomes (high level):
- Adaptive sampling prototype (route-level) deployed behind a feature flag; preliminary results show ~42% reduction in span count for the instrumented services with <3% loss in critical root-cause trace coverage on our alerting set.
- Identified two hotspots generating high-cardinality spans: embeddings-inference (debug traces left enabled) and the batch-rewrite worker. Both mitigations are straightforward: toggle debug off and add pre-filtering at the batch boundary.
- Dashboard migration: proof-of-concept export to Parquet in S3 using nightly compaction reduces dashboard query cost in dev by ~30% (p50 query CPU).

Decisions made:
- Proceed with expanding adaptive sampling to 10 additional routes next sprint (canary at 2% traffic per route). Owner: Tom.
- Add a small pre-ingest filter that drops low-utility spans with known noisy tags (session_heartbeat, heartbeat.v2) at the agent before they reach the tracer pipeline. Owner: Elena.
- Pause any further instrumentation of embeddings pipeline until debug-mode traces are gated by a runtime flag. Owner: Marcus.

Standup notes (Tue–Fri, condensed):
- Tue 2027-10-05: Aisha: validated sampling policy config format; found ambiguity in sampling priority field (fixed and updated schema). Tom: created canary rollout plan and traffic split experiments. Elena: initial pre-filter rules tested on staging; dropped 12% of spans (good). Marcus: triaged embedding debug traces; discovered an automated job enabling verbose logs during nightly runs (JAMAL-ops script).
- Wed 2027-10-06: Aisha: ran simulation with historical traces to check effect on alert recall; recall stayed at 97% for our 20 alert templates. Tom: deployed sampling flag to canary service cluster; telemetry showed expected drop. Priya: started dashboard query benchmark for columnar store.
- Thu 2027-10-07: Elena: pre-filter rule now at 95% test pass; one false-positive pattern found (internal-health-check spans) — added whitelist. Marcus: patch landed to gate embedding debug with env var; waiting on release. Jamal: SREs applied temporary quota to embedding jobs to limit trace bursts.
- Fri 2027-10-08: Tom: rollout postmortem draft for canary traffic split. Aisha: ran end-to-end test for alert pipeline with sampled traces; found one alert that regressed in recall (root cause: sampling of very short-lived DB spans) — created follow-up. Priya: export pipeline to parquet running; cost numbers baseline captured.

Metrics & Observations:
- Span ingestion delta (instrumented routes): -42% span volume week over week.
- Alert recall on monitored templates: 97% steady (one template regressed to 88% — see follow-up).
- Dashboard dev query CPU: -30% p50 after columnar migration POC.
- Unexpected telemetry spike: embedding pipeline caused short-lived ingestion surge (3x baseline) on 2027-10-05 03:00 UTC due to nightly debug enablement; cost impact estimated +12% for that billing day.

Follow-ups / Action items (owner, due):
- Aisha: write runbook section for adaptive-sampling toggles + rollback steps (due 2027-10-12).
- Tom: expand canary to 10 routes with staggered activation (due 2027-10-14). Include traffic-split monitors and automated rollback on alert drop below 90% recall.
- Elena: implement pre-ingest filter whitelist for internal-health-check spans and add unit tests (due 2027-10-11).
- Marcus: confirm embedding debug gating rollout to production and audit last 30 days for accidental debug enables (due 2027-10-13).
- Priya: finish full dashboard migration runbook and cost comparison doc (SLO: 20% cost improvement for long-term retention queries) (due 2027-10-18).
- Jamal / SRE: implement temporary soft cap on trace ingestion per-project to blunt emergency spikes (due 2027-10-09).
- A quick follow-up ticket created for the alert template that regressed: JIRA:OBS-4340 (owner Aisha).

Risks & open questions:
- Sampling edge-cases: very short DB spans (sub-ms) can be the only signal for some alert templates. Need a small exception list of span-types preserved regardless of sampling.
- Cost transfer risk: moving older metrics to Parquet lowers query CPU but increases storage egress and cold read costs in some partner clouds — need runbook to reconcile per-customer cost tradeoffs.
- Alerting SLA acceptance: product wants no more than 5% drop in recall for critical alerts. Can we guarantee that as sampling scales? We must finish the proof for 50 routes before making commitments.

Notes on instrumentation & mechanics:
- Sampling proto uses three levers: route-level target rate, priority override for spans tagged "root-cause-candidate", and time-bound emergency-preserve window (keeps all spans for 15s around a high-error burst).
- Pre-ingest filter implemented as a tiny WASM module in the agent with a deterministic whitelist check. Unit tests included in GH PR.
- Columnar migration is a nightly compaction job that writes daily parquet files partitioned by service and day; dashboards read a short-term cache for realtime and fall back to Parquet for historical slices.

Communication / stakeholder notes:
- Customer Success: alerted about possible small recall regression on one template; proactively preparing a short FAQ and mitigations list.
- Platform reliability: asked to review the SLO for trace ingestion soft caps.
- Sales / Enterprise: flagged that Private deployments may require different sampling defaults (customers with compliance needs may want full traces) — added note to product for config knobs.

Next sprint priorities (brief):
1) Canary expansion and monitoring automation for sampling (safety-first).
2) Harden pre-ingest filters with whitelist and better pattern matching.
3) Finish columnar migration runbook + start a pilot for one internal dashboard team.
4) Alert template remediation for regressed template and add unit tests to eval harness.

Notes-to-self / random observations:
- The embedding pipeline spike was noisy but instructive: we should add a nightly inhibitor that forces debug-mode off for long-running inference jobs unless explicitly requested.
- Consider a small 'always-preserve' set keyed by span.name hash for 0.1% of traffic to sample rare failure modes without blowing budget.

If anyone on the thread wants the raw telemetry CSVs or the Parquet POC dataset, ping me and I will drop links (small internal S3 bucket).

Appendix: quick link list (for reviewers)
- Canary rollout doc: GH PR /links/789 (see linked_artifacts)
- Simulation notebooks: GH:github.com/redwood-inference/observability/tree/main/notebooks/adaptive-sim
- Runbook draft: Confluence:OBS-adaptive-sampling-spike

End of digest.
